text:
camille: FYI, post-release canaries show OOMs on long-seqlen traffic (>=12k). Happening after the kernel-routing + autobatch merge.
ryan: Ugh. Which hosts / instance types? Logs?
camille: e2-standard-32 on canary pool A. Logs attached below, most fail during kv cache rebuild while streaming.
ci-bot: nightly-perf-tests: regression detected in `inference-longseq` (p99 latency +55%, mem peak +40%), test id `perf/longseq/2026-03-17`
vikram: Can you paste a representative OOM backtrace? Might be slab growth when prefetch and eviction interact.
camille: pastebin: https://paste.redwood/perf/3991234567-oom
camille: snippet of oom log:
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] Alloc failed: PageletAllocator::reserve(4096) -> out_of_memory
Stack: runtime::alloc_pagelet -> kv_cache::rehash -> prefetch::warmup -> kernel_router::dispatch
Active KV cache entries: 3.2M, slab fragmentation: 72%
```
dima: 72% frag is huge. That looks like small-chunk scattering after the kernel selection started favoring the new fused-attn kernel for mid-length sequences. That kernel's allocator path uses pagelet slices differently.
sam: Did we change eviction windows recently? There was a PR that moved eviction to be async with the allocator: PR #6281
jia: I ran a bisect yesterday between commits `main@{2026-03-15}` and `main@{2026-03-16}`. The regression landed around commit `a7c9f4d` (kernel-router: prefer fused-kernel when batch_size<=8). Repro steps I used:
```
# repro (on canary pool A)
./tools/run_inference_bench --model redwood/llama-13b --seq-length 14000 --batch 6 --workers 4 --profile=flame
```
jia: Attached flamegraph shows a widening in `kv_cache::rehash` and `PageletAllocator::scan_free` compared to baseline.
ryan: If kernel routing causes more small allocations, combined with our new async-evict timing it could turn into fragmentation cascade under long contexts.
vikram: Short-term mitigation: pin kernel routing to `legacy-kernel-v1` in canary config. That avoids the fused path.
camille: Can we hotfix a config pin and hold the rollout? I put the release on pause but need someone to push the pin.
sam: I can push a canary override. Will revert the router preference until we understand fragmentation pattern.
ciaction-bot: deploy-request by sam -> environment: canary-A -> change: kernel-router.pin=legacy-kernel-v1
ci-bot: canary tests queued: `perf/longseq` will re-run in ~12m
ryan: Also add a perf regression test that runs seq=12k/16k with mixed batch sizing; current CI only runs to 8k which missed this.
vikram: Agree. I'll add a test in perf-suite and tune eviction window to avoid synchronous rehash under load.
dima: For the bisect: I recommend instrumenting the allocator to produce an allocation histogram by size class (every 100ms sample) to see whether we get a spike in small-chunk churn after the kernel switch.
jia: Experiment results: when forcing fused kernel on baseline, small allocations <=512B increased 3.6x and fragmentation rose to 68% within 30s on longseq workloads.
camille: Ok. Plan: (1) sam pushes canary override (pin legacy kernel) right away. (2) hold rollout and revert PR `a7c9f4d` from next deploy unless we have patch. (3) vikram/dima add allocator histograms + perf test for seq>=12k. (4) ria: follow-up to see if async-evict timing needs backoff.
ryan: One more note: kernel selection logic also changed batching hints (it asked autobatcher to use smaller mini-batches for fused kernel). That reduced effective batch coalescing which likely reduced amortization of KV access patterns.
camille: Good catch — that matches flamegraph: more frequent `kv_cache::lookup` churn spikes.
sam: Pushing override now.
camille: :white_check_mark: thanks. Please post canary results when CI finishes.
ci-bot: canary perf/longseq re-run complete: p99 latency -2%, mem peak -35% compared to failing run, no OOMs in 1h smoke
camille: Great. Revert queued for `a7c9f4d` if we don't have a patch by EOD. Also adding postmortem label to the release PR.
ryan: Moving rollout to hold state and adding Triage channel thread.
vikram: I'll start on allocator instrumentation and a microbench to isolate fused kernel's allocation pattern.
jia: I'll attach the bisect data and flamegraphs to the incident ticket.
camille: Thanks everyone. Short retro after we stabilize.
